stored_per_answer.what: About five favourite things, chosen from a list (a kind and an identifier each, in the order chosen)
Optionally: a district, as a short place name
Optionally: a budget level from 1 to 4
Which poster was scanned, and the venue's survey it belongs to
The day, weekday and hour of the answer in the venue's own time (never the exact moment)
Which version of the consent text was shown
A quality flag: answers sent implausibly fast, or in a sudden burst at one poster, are held for review
The receipt code, kept only as a one-way hash, so a guest can delete their own answers
Which venue account the answer belongs to, and a random identifier for the answer itself

never: Names, email addresses, phone numbers or device identifiers.
The phone's location, or the guest's IP address, browser or exact time of answering.
Health, finances, politics or anything else sensitive.
Free text from a guest beyond a short district name.
rules: Groups under 10 people are never shown to an owner. A place or neighbourhood with fewer than 10 guests behind it is only a pin or a count.
Qloo results describe aggregate taste. They are never used to infer anything about a person.
Wording is about groups: “people who picked similar things also like”, never a prediction about you.
Qloo's facts are shown separately from our own interpretation, labelled measured, observed or modelled.
A guest can delete their own answers at any time with the receipt code. An owner can delete their account and its data.

The Qloo key stays on our server. What reaches Qloo from a guest is the words typed in the search box and the item chosen, with nothing that links them to the guest's answers; Qloo may keep and reuse them under its own terms, and the consent text says so.
A venue's own details (its name's kind, its position on the map) are sent to Qloo to find what is around it. They describe a business, not a person.
